title: Clinicopathological Determinants of Prognosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Integrating Histopathology with an IHC-Based Molecular Subclassification
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy that has undergone major therapeutic changes over the last two decades. Here, a real-world clinicopathological cohort integrating morphology, prognostic parameters, immunohistochemical surrogate markers for molecular stratification, and treatment outcome data is presented. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center study of 597 patients with histologically confirmed HCC (or occasional cases of combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) diagnosed at the Institute of Pathology, University of Regensburg, between 2000 and 2024. Clinical, pathological, laboratory, and follow-up data were merged with regional cancer registry data. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression. In a tissue microarray-based subcohort, immunohistochemistry for p53, Cyclin A2, Cyclin E1, β-catenin, and L-FABP1 was evaluated as a surrogate for a recently proposed molecular subclassification. Systemic treatment response and progression-free survival were assessed in patients with available follow-up data. Results The cohort comprised 486 men and 111 women, with a median age at diagnosis of 70 years in men and 67 years in women. Cirrhosis (49.7%), viral hepatitis (24.0%), diabetes mellitus (33.8%), arterial hypertension (45.2%), and steatosis hepatis (24.3%) were frequent background conditions. Median overall survival was 52 months. Survival declined with increasing grade and with incomplete resection. In multivariate Cox regression, older age, advanced T category, vascular invasion, positive resection margins, poor differentiation, macrotrabecular-massive (MTM) subtype, absence of tumor capsule, steatosis, and elevated alkaline phosphatase showed prognostic relevance, with age, T category, vascular invasion, resection status, MTM subtype, tumor capsule, and alkaline phosphatase emerging as particularly robust predictors. In the tissue microarray cohort, p53-high expression was independently associated with worse overall survival, whereas combined Cyclin A2/E1 high expression was significant in univariate analysis. L-FABP1 loss and nuclear β-catenin accumulation were not associated with outcome. Patients treated with atezolizumab/bevacizumab showed higher response rates than those treated with sorafenib. Conclusions This quarter-century single-center study highlights the multifactorial background, morphological diversity, and prognostic heterogeneity of HCC in routine clinical practice. Established clinicopathological variables remain the strongest determinants of survival, while p53 immunohistochemistry may provide additional prognostic information as an accessible molecular surrogate. The data further reflect the changing systemic treatment landscape from sorafenib to immunotherapy-based regimens in a real-world cohort.

title: Medical imaging in Bothrops lanceolatus envenomation: a retrospective series from Martinique
abstract: Abstract Background: Bothrops lanceolatus (Bl), a pit viper endemic to Martinique, is responsible for 40–50 envenomations annually. These are characterized by systemic thrombotic complications, that can lead to cerebral, myocardial, or pulmonary infarction. The introduction of the specific antivenom Bothrofav has substantially improved patient prognosis and management. Although severity grading remains primarily clinical, the specific role of medical imaging in this setting is underexplored. We aimed to delineate the contribution of imaging to the management of B. lanceolatus envenomation. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study at the University Hospital of Martinique from January 2011 to August 2024. All patients with documented B. lanceolatus envenomation were included. We collected data in imaging use, clinical severity grade, and complications. Bivariate analyses were performed to examine associations between clinical status and imaging use. Results: A total of 389 patients were included (median age 48 years [IQR 35–59]; 128 [33%] women). Seventy-nine patients (20%) underwent at least one imaging examination, for a total of 127 studies. Imaging was infrequently used in mild envenomation (Grades 1–2) but significantly more frequent in severe cases (Grades 3–4, p < 0.01) and then complications were present, including compartment syndrome, shock, coma, infection, or the need for surgery. Eleven thrombotic events were confirmed in six pa three cerebral infarctions, three myocardial infarctions, two pulmonary embolisms, and three deep vein thromboses. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) and Doppler ultrasound were central to the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism and peripheral thrombosis, respectively. Conclusions: Although the management of snakebite envenomation remains primarily clinical, judicious use of medical imaging, specifically CT, MRI, and Doppler ultrasound, serves as a valuable adjunct. Imaging enhances severity grading and is essential for confirming thrombotic complications, thereby supporting the development of standardized, imaging-based management protocols for B. lanceolatus envenomation.

title: Determinants of Access to Brain Tumor Care in Angola: A Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Background. Brain tumors require an exceptionally demanding continuum of care because clinical outcomes depend on timely recognition, neuroimaging, neurosurgical decision-making, pathology, oncology, radiotherapy, supportive treatment, and longitudinal follow-up. In low- and middle-income settings, this pathway is commonly disrupted by delays, out-of-pocket costs, urban concentration of services, and weak referral systems. Objective. To map the determinants of access to brain tumor care in Angola and to situate the Angolan context within the broader sub-Saharan African literature, with emphasis on clinical recognition, access to computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), neurosurgery, pathology, oncology, radiotherapy, financing, geography, continuity of care, and clinical governance. Methods. We conducted an exploratory scoping review of published and documentary sources, guided by PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. Indexed literature, African regional sources, clinical guidance documents, and institutional materials with analytic relevance to Angola were synthesized narratively according to major domains of access. Results. International and regional evidence indicates that brain tumor care is vulnerable to serial bottlenecks, including delayed presentation, initially nonspecific symptoms, diagnostic confusion with stroke, central nervous system infection, or epilepsy, inconsistent access to CT and MRI, specialist shortages, delayed surgery, limited pathology capacity, inadequate radiotherapy availability, and loss to follow-up. In Angola, disease-specific published evidence remains scarce, and the exact patient profile and care timelines are still insufficiently documented. Nevertheless, regional African literature and the minimum requirements of neuro-oncology suggest that access in Angola depends less on any single technical intervention than on the coordinated functioning of the entire diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conclusions. Access to brain tumor treatment in Angola should be framed as a systemic neuro-oncology challenge. Priority actions include strengthening clinical suspicion and referral pathways, ensuring functional CT and MRI access, protecting neurosurgical and anesthetic capacity, improving reliable pathology, integrating care with oncology and radiotherapy, expanding financial protection, and creating clinical registries capable of measuring delays, treatments, and outcomes.

title: Disease Spectrum Analysis and AI-Assisted Screening of Fundus Disorders Using Portable Handheld Fundus Imaging in Health Examination Populations
abstract: Abstract Objective: Portable handheld fundus imaging facilitates convenient population‑based eye screening, yet its clinical application is hindered by unstable image quality and insufficient real‑world population disease evidence. This study aimed to establish a feasible screening workflow for handheld fundus photography in physical examination cohorts, combining standardized image quality management, population fundus disease spectrum analysis, and intelligent auxiliary disease identification to support large‑scale eye health screening. Methods: A total of 58,500 non‑mydriatic handheld fundus images were consecutively collected from a tertiary general hospital health examination center between 2020 and 2025. Automated standardized quality assessment was performed to screen valid images for subsequent analyses. Qualified high‑quality images were included to analyze the distribution characteristics of fundus diseases in the general population. Meanwhile, a two‑stage intelligent auxiliary screening strategy was implemented to identify abnormal fundus images and further categorize specific types of abnormal fundus diseases. The screening and classification performance of multiple deep learning networks was comprehensively benchmarked on handheld fundus data. Results: The overall fundus abnormality rate of high‑quality images was 32.22%. Myopia‑related fundus changes (19.84%), retinal vascular diseases (5.89%), and macular diseases (3.82%) were the predominant abnormal fundus diseases in the examined population. Distinct age‑related distribution differences were observed: younger individuals were mainly affected by myopia‑related changes, whereas elderly populations had a higher burden of vascular and macular diseases. The established intelligent system achieved favorable performance in fundus abnormality screening (AUC = 0.9612) and fine‑grained abnormal disease classification (macro‑AUC = 0.8445). Lightweight models achieved favorable performance in handheld fundus image analysis. Retinal foundation models, pre‑trained on conventional adult fundus datasets, showed limited performance advantages in this portable imaging scenario. Conclusion: Standardized quality control and intelligent auxiliary analysis may support large‑scale multi‑disease fundus screening using portable handheld imaging in routine physical examinations. The observed age‑stratified distribution pattern of fundus diseases in this health examination population provides real‑world evidence for portable fundus screening. This study presents a practical framework for population‑level fundus health surveillance.

title: Comparison of One-Hole Split Endoscopy and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy for Far-Lateral Lumbar Disc Herniation at L5/S1: A Short-Term Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes between One-hole Split Endoscopy (OSE) and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) for L5/S1 far-lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH). Methods This retrospective study included 47 patients with L5-S1 FLLDH (July 2022-July 2024) divided into OSE and UBE groups. Surgical outcomes were documented. Radiographic parameters—including intervertebral foramen area (IVFA), height of the superior articular process (HSAP), lumbosacral lordotic angle (LLA), sagittal translation (ST), and disc height (DH)—were compared between groups. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Macnab criteria. Results Both groups exhibited significant improvement in VAS and ODI scores at all postoperative time points (P < 0.05), with no significant differences between groups. Excellent-to-good rates were 91.3% for OSE and 91.7% for UBE. One dural tear occurred in the OSE group. No significant intergroup differences were observed in any radiographic parameter. Postoperative ST and LLA remained stable (P > 0.05), whereas DH decreased, IVFA increased, and HSAP decreased (all P < 0.05). The UBE group demonstrated shorter operative time, while the OSE group had smaller incisions and less intraoperative blood loss. Conclusion Both UBE and OSE are effective minimally invasive approaches for treating L5-S1 FLLDH.

title: A Case Report and Literature Review of Extraskeletal Osteosarcoma of the Abdominal Wall
abstract: Abstract Background Extraskeletal osteosarcoma (ESOS) is a rare form of soft-tissue cancer characterized by the formation of osteoid matrix, bone, and cartilage. The clinical diagnosis has not been easy, and the prognosis is usually bad, with significant local recurrence rates and metastasis at a distance. The occurrence of ESOS in the abdominal wall is extremely uncommon. Case presentation: We present the case of a 60-year-old male who developed an enlarging mass in the lower right abdominal wall over 6 months with a local bulge and erythema, but without severe pain. Physical examination revealed a hard, non-tender mass measuring approximately 6 x 6 cm with indistinct margins but good mobility. Superficial ultrasonography indicated a primarily solid mass 59 x 53 x 39 mm. The operation was performed using wide surgical excision with general anesthesia. Intraoperative frozen section pathology revealed a mesenchymal soft tissue tumor, and this was confirmed by definitive histopathology with immunohistochemistry as ESOS. It is important to note that after surgery, the patient revealed that he had a history of thymoma, which had been treated with radiotherapy five years earlier; however, this information was initially not given. After surgery, the patient was given four courses of chemotherapy (cisplatin and ifosfamide) and radiation therapy. At 12-month follow-up, the surgical wound was well-healed, with no signs of local recurrence or new metastatic lesions. Conclusions Conclusively, ESOS of the abdominal wall is an uncommon and very malignant disease that tends to be misdiagnosed because of its non-specific clinical manifestations. This case demonstrates the significance of the extensive history-taking process, histopathological assessment with immunohistochemistry, and multimodal intervention approaches. The patient's prior radiotherapy underscores the need for a thorough clinical examination. This report adds to the sparse literature on ESOS of the abdomen and guides planning, early diagnosis, and treatment.

title: The AI-CDSS Evidence Gap: A Critical Analysis of Outcome Measurement, Human-AI Interaction, and Implementation Validation
abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) are increasingly promoted to improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making. However, questions remain about whether current evidence adequately demonstrates meaningful patient benefit. Existing research relies heavily on surrogate diagnostic metrics, provides limited insight into clinician–AI interaction, and rarely evaluates implementation in real-world healthcare settings. This review synthesizes evidence across these interconnected domains to identify critical gaps in AI-CDSS evaluation. Methods: A critical narrative review was conducted using the Grant and Booth (2009) review typology and thematic narrative synthesis. Literature published between January 2015 and May 2026 was searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and IEEE Xplore using three domains: clinical effectiveness, human–AI interaction, and implementation science. Relevant regulatory guidance and evaluation frameworks were identified through targeted searches of institutional and professional organization websites. Results: The search identified 1,247 records; following screening and eligibility assessment, 33 sources (28 peer-reviewed publications and five grey literature documents) were included. The strongest effectiveness evidence, a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomized controlled trials involving 12,657 participants, demonstrated only a small pooled effect (standardized mean difference 0.182; 95% CI 0.003–0.362; GRADE: moderate), with all trials measuring diagnostic accuracy rather than patient-centred outcomes such as mortality or length of stay. Most studies originated from East Asia and focused on radiology, limiting generalizability. Human factors evidence identified significant vulnerabilities, including automation bias that reduced diagnostic accuracy among inexperienced radiologists when incorrect AI recommendations were presented, high false-positive alarm rates promoting alert fatigue, and limited clinician scrutiny of erroneous AI outputs. Although evaluation and implementation frameworks, including CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, CFIR, and RE-AIM, have been developed, prospective validation remains limited, with almost no implementation evidence from sub-Saharan Africa or other low- and middle-income countries. Conclusion: Current AI-CDSS evidence inadequately captures real-world effectiveness and unintended harms. Future research should prioritize patient-centred outcomes, rigorous evaluation of clinician–AI interaction, and prospective validation of implementation frameworks across diverse healthcare settings. Strengthening evidence standards, including fairness and equity considerations, is essential for the safe, effective, and scalable deployment of AI-CDSS.

The search identified 1,247 records; following screening and eligibility assessment, 33 sources (28 peer-reviewed publications and five grey literature documents) were included. The strongest effectiveness evidence, a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomized controlled trials involving 12,657 participants, demonstrated only a small pooled effect (standardized mean difference 0.182; 95% CI 0.003–0.362; GRADE: moderate), with all trials measuring diagnostic accuracy rather than patient-centred outcomes such as mortality or length of stay. Most studies originated from East Asia and focused on radiology, limiting generalizability. Human factors evidence identified significant vulnerabilities, including automation bias that reduced diagnostic accuracy among inexperienced radiologists when incorrect AI recommendations were presented, high false-positive alarm rates promoting alert fatigue, and limited clinician scrutiny of erroneous AI outputs. Although evaluation and implementation frameworks, including CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, CFIR, and RE-AIM, have been developed, prospective validation remains limited, with almost no implementation evidence from sub-Saharan Africa or other low- and middle-income countries.

Conclusion:

Current AI-CDSS evidence inadequately captures real-world effectiveness and unintended harms. Future research should prioritize patient-centred outcomes, rigorous evaluation of clinician–AI interaction, and prospective validation of implementation frameworks across diverse healthcare settings. Strengthening evidence standards, including fairness and equity considerations, is essential for the safe, effective, and scalable deployment of AI-CDSS.

title: Low-Dose Esketamine Combined with Propofol for Sedation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Bidirectional Endoscopy: A single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Sedation for same-visit bidirectional gastrointestinal endoscopy in elderly patients remains a major clinical challenge. Propofol monotherapy carries a prominent risk of respiratory and circulatory depression, particularly in geriatric patients with limited physiological reserve. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, exerts sympathomimetic effects that may offset propofol-induced hypotension and hypoxaemia. However, high-quality clinical evidence in this specific population is insufficient. This trial evaluated whether low-dose esketamine added to propofol reduces cardiopulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing bidirectional endoscopy. Methods In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, 316 elective patients aged 60–80 years with ASA physical status I–III were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive either intravenous esketamine 0.15 mg/kg or normal saline placebo, followed by propofol 1 mg/kg for sedation induction. The dual primary outcomes were the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia. Prespecified secondary outcomes included procedural efficiency and quality indicators. Results The overall incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia showed no significant intergroup differences. However, patients in the esketamine group maintained more stable intraoperative systolic blood pressure (SBP) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SPO₂) throughout the procedure. Esketamine also demonstrated superior procedural efficiency: shorter median induction time (120 s vs. 140 s; P < 0.001), 16.7% lower median propofol consumption (125 mg vs. 150 mg; P < 0.001), and 100% first-attempt gastroscope insertion success versus 94.9% with placebo (P = 0.007). Intraoperative bucking was halved (6.3% vs. 13.9%; P = 0.039). These gains were not offset by increased adverse events, including psychotomimetic effects, nausea and vomiting, dizziness, or cognitive impairment. Recovery times and patient satisfaction remained similarly high. Conclusions In conclusion, adjuvant low-dose esketamine combined with propofol did not reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension or hypoxemia in elderly patients undergoing same-visit bidirectional endoscopy. However, intraoperative SBP and SpO₂ were better preserved in patients receiving esketamine during the whole procedure. This regimen provided multiple clinical benefits including shortened induction time, higher first-pass gastroscopy insertion success rate, lower propofol dosage and reduced intraoperative bucking, without increasing overall adverse event risks. Trial registration Trial registration: This trial was prospectively registered on 26 March 2025 in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registration number ChiCTR2500099643; https://www.chictr.org.cn/).

title: Lichen Sclerosus, Breast Cancer, and the Impact of Hormonal Therapy: A Large-Scale Propensity-Matched Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the bidirectional association between lichen sclerosus and breast cancer, and to assess whether hormonal breast cancer therapies influence the subsequent risk of developing lichen sclerosus. Methods: This retrospective cohort study utilized a global electronic health record network containing over 204 million patients. Female patients with lichen sclerosus were compared to matched controls with postmenopausal atrophic vaginitis. Reciprocally, breast cancer patients were compared to matched controls who underwent mammography without a cancer diagnosis. Cohorts were propensity-score matched for age, race, ethnicity, body mass index, and smoking status. Results: Among 77,386 patients with lichen sclerosus and 77,163 controls, lichen sclerosus was associated with a lower incidence of subsequent breast cancer (2.22% vs. 2.55%; RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.93, p<0.001). Conversely, in 563,498 breast cancer patients without hormonal therapy versus 563,676 controls, breast cancer was associated with a higher incidence of subsequent lichen sclerosus (0.18% vs. 0.10%; RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.67-2.04, p<0.001). Hormonal therapy exposure in breast cancer patients showed a minimal risk increase for lichen sclerosus (RR 1.07, p=0.031), with no significant association found for tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors specifically. Conclusion: Lichen sclerosus is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, whereas breast cancer is associated with a higher subsequent incidence of lichen sclerosus. Because this increased risk persists in patients who did not receive hormonal therapy, mechanisms beyond estrogen deprivation likely drive the development of lichen sclerosus in breast cancer patients.

title: Extreme Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor–Associated Thrombocytosis with Concurrent C-MET Upregulation Evolution in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) carries a dismal prognosis. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have modestly improved survival, but durable responses are uncommon, and hematologic immune-related adverse events (irAEs)—<1% of treated patients—remain poorly characterised. Extreme reactive thrombocytosis (> 1,000 × 10⁹/L) has not been documented during ICI therapy for ES-SCLC, and its mechanism and management are undefined. Endocrine irAEs (secondary adrenal insufficiency) are increasingly recognised, but their concurrence with hematologic toxicity has not been described. Case Presentation. A 62-year-old man with ES-SCLC received first-line Toripalimab-based immunotherapy. On day 71 (24 February 2026), the platelet count peaked at 1,033 × 10⁹/L, prompting urgent therapeutic plateletpheresis. Concurrent serology showed interferon-γ approximately 45 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), ferritin approximately 20× ULN, and elevated soluble interleukin-2 receptor, consistent with an incomplete hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) phenotype. C-reactive protein peaked at 178.40 mg/L and interleukin-6 reached 199.68 pg/mL on 2 March 2026, supporting cytokine-driven myeloproliferation. Serial tumor biopsies documented C-MET evolution from 10% weak-positive to 80% strong-positive. Early tumor shrinkage (11% reduction from a 118-mm baseline) coincided with the platelet peak on day 71, while maximal radiographic response (50% reduction) was achieved on day 121 (15 April 2026). Treatment was modified with antiangiogenic optimization (Anlotinib 12 mg daily) and Toripalimab was substituted with Tislelizumab. Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (PTV 45 Gy/25 fractions, PGTV 50 Gy/25 fractions, simultaneous integrated boost) commenced on 23 May 2026. On the same day, endocrinology consultation confirmed secondary adrenal insufficiency (ACTH < 0.22 pmol/L, cortisol < 2.76 nmol/L), managed with prednisolone replacement and blood pressure restoration. Conclusions. The temporal sequence—peak platelet count (day 71) preceding maximal tumor response (day 121) implicates immune activation, not tumor burden, as the thrombocytosis driver. C-MET upregulation under PD-1 blockade may represent both a resistance mechanism and a targetable salvage pathway. This first reported concurrence of extreme thrombocytosis, incomplete HLH, and secondary adrenal insufficiency in a single ES-SCLC patient underscores the need for multi-system irAE monitoring. Trial Registration Clinical trial number: not applicable. This is a retrospective single-patient case report; no prospective clinical trial was conducted, and no patient was enrolled in a registered clinical trial for the treatments described.

title: Prediction of LN-prRLN Metastasis in cN0 PTMC Patients Using Logistic Regression and Machine Learning: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) is steadily increasing, with metastasis to lymph nodes posterior to the right recurrent laryngeal nerve (LN-prRLN) occurring in 7.1% to 34.9% of cases. Preoperative ultrasound fails to detect most LN-prRLN metastases. Accurate risk assessment of LN-prRLN in clinically node-negative (cN0) PTMC patients is essential for determining the appropriate surgical extent and evaluating the feasibility of active surveillance. Objective To develop and compare logistic regression and machine learning models for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients, thereby supporting individualized preoperative and intraoperative clinical decision-making. Methods A total of 1051 cN0 PTMC patients were retrospectively analyzed and randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Clinical, ultrasonographic, and pathological variables were collected. Using LN-prRLN metastasis status as the endpoint, logistic regression and multiple machine learning models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), calibration curves, and precision-recall curves. The best-performing machine learning model was compared with the logistic model, and SHAP values were employed for model interpretability. Results Multivariate logistic regression identified anterior prelaryngeal lymph node metastatic ratio (LNMR) and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR as independent predictors of LN-prRLN metastasis. Among machine learning algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the best discriminative ability and calibration stability. Although XGBoost yielded higher area under the ROC curve (AUC) values than the logistic model in both training and validation sets, the difference was not statistically significant. SHAP analysis revealed that anterior prelaryngeal LNMR and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR were the two most influential predictors, contributing cumulatively over 66% to the prediction with strong interaction effects. Other notable contributors included anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve lymph node metastasis, prelaryngeal lymph node metastasis, tumor size, left central compartment LNMR, capsular invasion, age, left central compartment lymph node metastasis, and multifocality. Conclusion Both logistic regression and machine learning models are reliable tools for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients. Integrating these models can assist clinicians in accurately identifying high-risk patients preoperatively or intraoperatively, enabling more patient-centered clinical decisions.

title: OCT evaluation as a prognostic indicator for management of macular edema secondary to venous occlusion treated with Ranibizumab
abstract: Abstract Aim: To study OCT characteristics as a prognostic guide in macular edema secondary to non-ischemic central retinal vein occlusion treated with intravitreal Ranibizumab Materials and methods: 60 patients with macular edema secondary to non-ischemic central retinal vein occlusion treated with Ranibizumab OCT analyzed on pattern of macular edema, reflectivity of outer band of photoreceptor-RPE complex. Its bearing on visual prognosis was analyzed. RESULTS: Good reflectivity of outer layer is a good prognostic feature. Cystoid pattern is a better prognostic indicator than sub retinal fluid Conclusion: The type of macular edema and reflectivity of third high reflectivity band before treatment can be predictive of visual outcome

title: A Simplified Surgical Bypass for Complete Afferent Loop Obstruction After Pancreaticoduodenectomy Guided by Afferent Loop Length: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Recurrent afferent loop obstruction (ALO) after pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is a challenging clinical problem. When tumor recurrence leads to complete occlusion with failure of guidewire passage, endoscopic interventions are rarely successful. Although percutaneous transhepatic cholangial drainage (PTCD) can provide emergency decompression, it requires permanent external drainage, leading to digestive fluid loss and decreased quality of life. While surgical bypass is a recognized principle, the anatomical prerequisites that determine its feasibility—particularly the available length of the proximal afferent loop—have not been systematically addressed. This report aims to fill this gap by proposing an experience-based reference for patient selection based on loop length and presenting long-term quality-of-life data. Case Presentation: A 72-year-old male developed complete ALO due to pancreatic cancer recurrence 7 months after PD. Preoperative assessment showed a single-site obstruction and a sufficiently long proximal afferent loop (>50 cm, intraoperative estimation), which enabled a direct, tension-free side-to-side anastomosis between the proximal afferent loop and the distal jejunum without Roux-en-Y reconstruction. Results: Symptoms resolved within 48 hours postoperatively. Total bilirubin decreased from 156 μmol/L to 34 μmol/L by postoperative day 7. GIQLI score increased from 28 preoperatively to 52 at 3 months. No recurrent obstruction occurred during 6-month follow-up. The patient died 9 months postoperatively due to widespread metastases. Conclusion: For carefully selected patients with complete recurrent ALO after PD in whom endoscopy is not feasible, afferent loop jejunal anastomosis appears safe and effective. Based on our experience, a proximal afferent loop length >50 cm and a single-site obstruction are favorable anatomical conditions allowing simplified direct anastomosis without complex Roux-en-Y reconstruction. However, these criteria represent a single-surgeon experience and require validation in larger cohorts.

title: Computed Tomography Outcomes After Frozen Elephant Trunk for Type A Dissection: Single-Branched Versus Straight Stent Grafts
abstract: Abstract Background To compare short-term computed tomography angiography (CTA) findings after frozen elephant trunk (FET) for type A aortic dissection (TAAD) using a single-branched stent graft (Fontus) versus a straight stent graft (Cronus). Methods A single-center retrospective study (July 1, 2021 – August 31, 2024) included 189 TAAD patients (Fontus, n = 111; Cronus, n = 78) after excluding anatomical contraindications. Postoperative CTA assessed branch endoleak, stented-segment false lumen thrombosis, and distal stent-induced new entry (dSINE). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline differences. Results Stented-segment false lumen thrombosis was comparable between Fontus and Cronus, indicating non-inferior performance of the branched design. In the Fontus cohort, branch-related endoleak occurred in 11 patients (10%) and was independently associated with left subclavian artery (LSA) involvement by dissection (odds ratio, 11.24; P = 0.003). Branch endoleak delayed complete thrombosis but did not alter mid-term remodeling. dSINE incidence did not differ by stent type but was independently driven by distal stent angulation (hazard ratio, 2.27 per 10°; P < 0.01); angles exceeding 30° were particularly hazardous. Conclusions Short-term CTA outcomes after FET for TAAD are comparable between Fontus and Cronus. Branch endoleak (10%) is the principal imaging limitation of the single-branched strategy and is predicted by LSA dissection involvement; thus, careful preoperative LSA assessment is advised. Across both stent types, distal angulation > 30° independently predicts dSINE, emphasizing the need for intraoperative geometric alignment and rigorous postoperative CTA surveillance.

title: MRI Evidence of Anterograde Trans-synaptic Degeneration After Eye Loss: Preserved Primary Visual Cortex Thickness Despite Lateral Geniculate Nucleus Atrophy
abstract: Abstract Background: Anterograde trans-synaptic degeneration (ATD) of the visual pathway following eye loss is well recognized, but its in vivo characterization remains limited. We investigated structural changes in the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) and primary visual cortex (V1) using automated analysis of high-resolution 3-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods: This cross-sectional study included 30 patients with unilateral or bilateral eye loss (≥6 months after enucleation or evisceration) and 75 healthy controls. All participants underwent standardized 3-T brain MRI. Automated LGN segmentation and cortical parcellation were performed using FreeSurfer version 7.2. Bilateral LGN volumes and mean V1 cortical thickness were compared between groups, and the relationship between LGN volume and time since eye loss was assessed. Results: Patients showed significantly smaller bilateral LGN volumes than controls (both p < 0.001). No significant association was found between LGN volume and time since eye loss, suggesting that most LGN atrophy develops early after visual deprivation. In contrast, mean V1 cortical thickness did not differ significantly between patients and controls (left hemisphere: p = 0.704; right hemisphere: p = 0.106). Conclusions: Eye loss is associated with marked bilateral LGN atrophy, but no significant reduction in V1 cortical thickness was detected with the methodology used, suggesting differential susceptibility of subcortical and cortical visual structures to ATD. Automated analysis of high-resolution 3-T MRI provides a practical, non-invasive method for investigating structural changes of the visual pathway in vivo.

title: NeviUNet: An Efficient Attention-Enhanced Network for Skin Lesion Segmentation in Total Body Images
abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the challenge of efficient and accurate automated segmentation of skin lesions in total body photographyacquired under clinical conditions. The study utilizes an image dataset captured via a prototype Dermo Studio total-bodyscanner designed for multi-perspective documentation of the patient’s skin surface. To balance segmentation accuracy withcomputational efficiency, a modified deep neural network architecture based on the U-Net model is proposed. The networkintegrates selected design enhancements inspired by ResUNet++, including the Mish activation function, Attention Gates,and SE blocks, while omitting computationally expensive residual connections and ASPP modules. To mitigate severe classimbalance, a composite loss function combining Focal Tversky Loss and BCE was employed. Quantitative evaluation onan independent test dataset demonstrated the superiority of the proposed approach, securing a mean DSC of 0.729 andsignificantly outperforming the baseline configurations. The proposed architecture features low inference latency and optimizedhardware resource allocation, confirming its suitability for deployment in real-time clinical medical devices.

title: Postpartum Necrotizing Fasciitis with Unilateral Foot Gangrene in an Adolescent After Unsupervised Home Vaginal Delivery: A Case Re
abstract: Abstract Background Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly progressive soft-tissue infection associated with substantial morbidity, limb loss, and mortality when diagnosis and surgical treatment are delayed. Postpartum necrotizing fasciitis is rare and is most commonly reported following cesarean delivery, episiotomy, or perineal infection. Distal lower-limb involvement with unilateral foot gangrene after vaginal delivery is particularly unusual. Case presentation A 15-year-old previously healthy postpartum adolescent from a rural community presented approximately two weeks after an unsupervised home vaginal delivery with progressive right lower-limb pain, swelling, foul-smelling discharge, inability to ambulate, and black discoloration of the right foot. On admission, she appeared critically ill and markedly pale. Laboratory investigations showed severe anemia with a hemoglobin concentration of approximately 4 g/dL, a C-reactive protein concentration of 70 mg/L, a white blood cell count of 7,000/µL, and coagulopathy with an international normalized ratio of 2.0. Computed tomography demonstrated extensive soft-tissue gas in the right foot and a posterior calf intramuscular abscess extending toward the plantar foot. Computed tomography angiography showed preserved major arterial flow without major arterial occlusion. Deep tissue cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli . The patient underwent resuscitation, packed red blood cell transfusion, correction of coagulopathy, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic therapy, serial surgical debridements, and right transmetatarsal amputation for irreversible forefoot gangrene. Negative-pressure wound therapy was used to promote granulation tissue formation. During the fourth week of hospitalization, definitive closure of the transmetatarsal stump and skin grafting of the posterior ankle/Achilles soft-tissue defect were performed. Infection was controlled, wound healing was satisfactory, and limb function proximal to the amputation level was preserved at discharge. Infection was controlled, wound healing was satisfactory, and limb function proximal to the amputation level was preserved at discharge. At the 1-month postoperative follow-up, the transmetatarsal amputation stump and posterior ankle/Achilles wound remained satisfactorily healed without wound breakdown or clinical evidence of recurrent infection. Conclusions Postpartum necrotizing fasciitis should be considered in patients presenting with rapidly progressive limb pain, swelling, skin necrosis, or gangrene, even after vaginal delivery and in the absence of leukocytosis or major arterial occlusion. Early resuscitation, correction of physiological abnormalities, culture-guided antimicrobial therapy, aggressive surgical source control, and staged wound reconstruction are essential for controlling infection and preserving functional limb length.

title: Transient Acquired Speech Dysfluency Temporally Associated with Dexmedetomidine- Assisted Sedation During Spinal Anesthesia: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Dexmedetomidine (DEX), a highly selective α₂-adrenoceptor agonist, is widely used for perioperative sedation because it provides cooperative sedation while maintaining spontaneous respiration and reducing the risk of respiratory depression. Although its pharmacological characteristics and safety profile have been extensively investigated, neurological adverse events involving speech production remain rarely reported. We describe a case of transient acquired speech dysfluency temporally associated with dexmedetomidine-assisted sedation during spinal anesthesia. Case Presentation A 63-year-old woman (American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II) underwent elective arthroscopic surgery of the left knee under spinal anesthesia. Dexmedetomidine was administered for intraoperative sedation using a loading infusion followed by continuous maintenance infusion. Approximately 30 minutes after discontinuation of dexmedetomidine, the patient suddenly developed difficulty initiating speech characterized by repetition of initial sounds and syllables and sound prolongation. She remained fully conscious and oriented throughout the episode, with preserved comprehension, naming ability, semantic expression, and articulation. Neurological examination revealed no focal neurological deficits except for the speech abnormality, corresponding to a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 1. Brain magnetic resonance imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, and intracranial magnetic resonance angiography demonstrated no evidence of acute cerebral infarction or major intracranial vascular abnormalities. No specific neurological treatment was administered. The speech disturbance resolved spontaneously approximately 97 minutes after symptom onset. The patient recovered completely without recurrence during hospitalization or the 7-day follow-up period. Conclusions This case describes transient acquired speech dysfluency occurring in close temporal association with dexmedetomidine-assisted sedation during spinal anesthesia. Although a causal relationship cannot be established from a single case, dexmedetomidine-related modulation of speech-associated neural networks may represent one possible explanation, particularly in patients with pre-existing basal ganglia abnormalities. Acute cerebrovascular events should always be excluded when new-onset speech abnormalities occur during the perioperative period.

title: Imaging Performance of a Stationary Tomography Baggage Scanner with Downward π-Angle Sparsity
abstract: Abstract This study introduces a novel stationary tomography baggage scanner that employs a downward π-angle configuration to enhance image quality under sparse-view conditions. Although stationary computed tomography (CT) systems offer mechanical simplicity and high throughput, the limited number of projections poses a challenge to image reconstruction. To address this, we investigated four angular configurations by reconstructing images using a compressed sensing (CS)-based iterative algorithm and conducted comprehensive evaluations of the image quality through various quantitative metrics. Using a realistic numerical phantom, the CS-based reconstruction consistently surpassed conventional filtered backprojection based reconstruction across all configurations, demonstrating improved image quality. Among the designs tested, a non-uniform π-angle configuration provided the most efficient angular sampling, yielding superior image quality as confirmed by ray distribution analysis, sinogram characteristics, and three quantitative metrics. These results demonstrate that geometric optimization coupled with advanced reconstruction can substantially improve imaging performance in sparse-view baggage screening systems.

title: Development and External Validation of a Risk Score for Post-Appendectomy Intra-Abdominal Infection
abstract: Abstract Background. Intra-abdominal infection (IAI) following appendectomy is a serious complication associated with prolonged hospitalization, repeated interventions, and increased morbidity. No universally accepted risk-stratification tool exists to guide individualized perioperative management or antimicrobial stewardship decisions after appendectomy. Objective. To identify independent preoperative and intraoperative predictors of post-appendectomy IAI and to develop a simple, clinically usable risk-stratification score to support perioperative decision-making and tailored antibiotic strategies. Methods. A retrospective analytical cohort study conducted at the General Surgery Department, CTGB, Ben Arous, Tunisia, over 24 months (January 2023–December 2023). All patients aged ≥ 14 years operated on for confirmed acute appendicitis were included. IAI was defined as a symptomatic intra-abdominal collection confirmed by imaging and/or drainage within 30 postoperative days. Univariate analysis and parsimonious multivariate logistic regression were performed. A bedside risk score (IAI-Risk Score) was derived from independent predictors and internally validated by stratification. Results. Of 400 patients (median age 32 years; 55% male), IAI occurred in 12 cases (3.0%). Four independent predictors were identified by parsimonious multivariate analysis: appendiceal peritonitis (aOR 5.12; 95% CI 3.54–9.42; p = 0.001), elevated CRP > 80.5 mg/L (aOR 4.22; 95% CI 1.60–14.87; p = 0.001), gangrenous appendicitis (aOR 2.22; 95% CI 1.52–4.28; p = 0.028), and appendicolith on CT (aOR 1.82; 95% CI 1.38–8.80; p = 0.001). CRP demonstrated excellent discriminative performance (AUC 0.892; 95% CI 0.827–0.958). The derived IAI-Risk Score stratified patients into low- (0%), intermediate- (5.4%), and high-risk (40.0%) groups. External validation in an independent cohort of 200 patients confirmed acceptable discriminative performance of the IAI-Risk Score (AUC 0.801; 95% CI [0.701–0.901]), supporting its generalizability beyond the derivation center. Conclusion. A parsimonious perioperative risk model combining inflammatory, radiological, and intraoperative parameters allows reliable stratification of post-appendectomy IAI risk. CRP > 80.5 mg/L, appendicolith, gangrenous appendicitis, and appendiceal peritonitis should trigger intensified postoperative surveillance and risk-adapted antibiotic strategies, supporting contemporary antimicrobial stewardship principles. External validation confirmed adequate generalizability of the score, supporting its integration into risk-adapted perioperative antibiotic and surveillance protocols after appendectomy.

title: Preserved consciousness as a diagnostic pitfall: a case report of tramadol-induced serotonin syndrome with isolated neuromuscular symptoms in an adolescent after general anesthesia
abstract: Abstract Background Serotonin syndrome (SS) typically presents with altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and neuromuscular abnormalities. We report an atypical case of perioperative tramadol-induced SS in an adolescent characterized by isolated neuromuscular symptoms with completely preserved consciousness and stable autonomic function, challenging the established paradigm that altered mental status and hyperthermia are obligatory for diagnosis. Case presentation: A 13-year-old girl (54 kg,body mass index 23.4 kg/m²) underwent arthroscopic meniscus repair under general anesthesia with fentanyl. One hour postoperatively, tramadol 50 mg (0.93 mg/kg) was administered intravenously. Ten minutes later, she developed right-hand tremor progressing to bilateral paroxysmal convulsions. Crucially, she remained fully conscious, coherent, and oriented throughout, accurately recalling the convulsive process. Continuous monitoring revealed stable hemodynamics without hyperthermia (maximal temperature 37.2°C). Emergent non-contrast head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed no structural abnormalities. Blood gas analysis showed metabolic acidosis (lactate 6.0 mmol/L) and electrolyte disturbances. After midazolam sedation and electrolyte correction, symptoms recurred. Multidisciplinary consultation and Hunter criteria application confirmed SS. Treatment included tramadol discontinuation, midazolam infusion, and supportive care, leading to symptom resolution within 3 days. Conclusions This case represents a rare abortive form of SS characterized by isolated neuromuscular manifestations without autonomic or mental status changes. Anesthesiologists should not exclude SS based on intact mental status or normothermia; Hunter criteria should be applied immediately when abnormal neuromuscular symptoms occur postoperatively in patients with recent serotonergic drug exposure. The proposed cortico-spinal dissociation mechanism may explain this consciousness-sparing phenotype, though it requires further validation.

title: Multi-Expert Measurement-Aware Learning for Carotid Intima-Media Complex Segmentation and Thickness Quantification in Ultrasound Images
abstract: Abstract Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is widely used as an ultrasound biomarker for evaluating vascular wall remodeling and early atherosclerotic changes. Reliable CIMT quantification requires accurate delineation of the far-wall intima-media complex (IMC), together with precise identification of the lumen-intima (LI) and media-adventitia (MA) interfaces. In clinical carotid B-mode ultrasound, however, IMC segmentation remains challenging because images are commonly degraded by speckle artifacts, weak contrast, and indistinct tissue boundaries. Moreover, annotations provided by different experts may vary in boundary placement, local thickness estimation, and labeled spatial extent, which can weaken the robustness of models trained under single-rater supervision. To reduce the influence of such annotation variability, this study develops a multi-expert measurement-aware learning framework for carotid IMC segmentation and IMT quantification. Based on the three expert annotations, A1, A1′, and A2, available in the technical version of the CUBS dataset, the proposed framework retains multi-expert supervisory information throughout training, enabling the model to learn more stable and representative IMC features. In addition, a measurement-aware loss is introduced to associate the LI and MA boundaries derived from the predicted mask with the resulting IMT error, thereby guiding the model toward both region-level segmentation accuracy and millimeter-scale thickness measurement precision. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive IMC segmentation performance while producing a near-zero measurement bias of -0.0024 mm and strong absolute agreement with an ICC of 0.7268. These findings suggest that multi-expert measurement-aware learning offers an effective way to align IMC segmentation with the final IMT quantification target under multi-rater annotation variability, supporting more reliable automated carotid ultrasound measurement.

title: Clinically Diagnosed Diamond-Blackfan Anemia with Negative Whole Exome Sequencing in an Infant with Crossed Renal Ectopia: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a rare congenital bone marrow failure syndrome presenting with early-onset anemia and reticulocytopenia. Approximately 30–40% of clinically typical cases remain genetically unresolved on exome sequencing, and a diagnosis can still be established on clinical and morphological grounds when the phenotype is characteristic. Case presentation: We report an 80-day-old female infant of non-consanguineous parentage who presented with pallor, poor feeding, and severe transfusion-dependent anemia with reticulocytopenia since birth. Bone marrow examination showed a normocellular marrow with marked erythroid paucity and an elevated myeloid-to-erythroid ratio, with adequate megakaryocytes and no fibrosis or malignancy. Whole exome sequencing targeting RPS19, GATA1, and TSR2 was non-diagnostic, revealing only a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in KMT2D. Contrast-enhanced CT urography incidentally identified a non-fused crossed ectopic left kidney. Alternative nutritional, infectious, and inherited marrow failure causes were excluded, and a clinical diagnosis of DBA was made. The infant was managed with packed red blood cell transfusion and supportive care. Conclusion This case illustrates that DBA can be diagnosed on clinical and morphological grounds despite a negative exome sequencing result, and describes non-fused crossed renal ectopia as an anomaly not previously reported in association with DBA, broadening the recognized spectrum of congenital anomalies in this disorder.

title: Enhanced anti-tumor efficacy of Electrochemotherapy combined with marginal surgery in dogs with Mast Cell Tumors and Soft Tissue Sarcomas
abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Electrochemotherapy (ECT) has emerged as an effective treatment modality for various tumor types in both preclinical and clinical settings within human and veterinary Oncology. We sought to evaluate the effect of electrochemotherapy (ECT) on survival of companion dogs with mast cell tumors and soft tissue sarcomas as an adjuvant to surgery. Materials and Methods A single-institution retrospective case series evaluation was used to identify dogs with mast cell tumors and soft tissue sarcomas undergoing surgical resection followed by electrochemotherapy from 2020–2024. Patients were selected based on having both therapies and categorized by histopathology. ECT was combined post-surgery with IV bleomycin and IL cisplatin in all cases. Overall response rate, survival and recurrence was analyzed. Results A total of 605 patients were identified as having surgery with incomplete margins followed by electrochemotherapy with either a diagnosis of mast cell tumor or soft tissue sarcoma. Grade was determined for all patients and recurrence free survival was stratified according to grade. Three hundred thirty-one dogs with mast cell tumor were retrospectively evaluated and two hundred and seventy-four dogs with soft tissue sarcoma were evaluated. This study obtained local control in both cutaneous and subcutaneous mast cell tumors as well as soft tissue sarcomas. The mean progression free interval in cutaneous mast cell tumors was 1825 days for grade I, 1803 days for low grade II, 902 days for high grade II and 817 days for grade III. Subcutaneous mast cell tumors were evaluated to be 1814 days for low grade and 1180 days for high grade. The mean progression free interval soft tissue sarcomas were 1432 days for grade I, 1000 days in grade II and 551 days in grade III respectively. Necrosis was observed at an average rate of 22% in mast cell tumors and in 18% of soft tissue sarcomas. Conclusion In this large study, electrochemotherapy decreased local recurrences after incomplete resection from surgery. The majority of publications are from European countries and this is the first evaluation of a large cohort of cases from the United States able to define overall progression free interval according to grade. Electrochemotherapy can offer a localized mechanism of control with minimal toxicity and continued use of this therapy is warranted in other tumor types.

title: NACS-Net: Normality–Anatomy–Concept Segmentation for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer on T2-Weighted MRI
abstract: Abstract Segmentation of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) on T2-weighted (T2W) MRI2remains difficult for three reasons. First, lesions occupy a very small fraction of each3scan, and most slices contain no lesion, creating severe foreground–background imbalance.4Second, csPCa often appears as a subtle, low-contrast deviation from surrounding tissue,5especially when only the T2W sequence is available. Third, models trained at a single6institution often lose accuracy on data acquired with different scanners and protocols. We propose NACS-Net, a segmentation framework that adapts a frozen vision foundation8model with lightweight trainable adapters and couples three components to address these9challenges. A normality–deviation dual-stream learns the appearance of normal prostate10tissue from abundant lesion-free regions and produces a feature-space deviation map that11highlights candidate lesions. An anatomy-gated iterative refinement decoder sharpens the12prediction over multiple loops, with each loop spatially constrained by an automatically13obtained 2D DynUNet gland mask to suppress extra-glandular false positives. A sparse14concept bottleneck encodes the lesion representation into a small set of candidate concepts,15intended to regularize the representation and support post-hoc inspection; their clinical16semantics require expert validation. NACS-Net is evaluated using patient-level five-fold17cross-validation on PI-CAI together with the official fixed training/validation split of18Prostate158, and external robustness is evaluated on an independent cohort (Prostate-19MRI-US-Biopsy). Across five internal evaluation runs, NACS-Net attains a mean Dice of2044.4±1.8, an HD95 of15.92±1.28mm, and4.48±0.33false positives per case. On the21unseen external cohort, it attains a Dice of23.5±3.8and an HD95 of24.66±1.41mm; the22cohort contains only positive cases, so external case-level ranking metrics are not defined. Ablations indicate that the normality–deviation stream, anatomy-gated refinement, and24sparse bottleneck each affect complementary aspects of performance, although the clinical25semantics of the learned concepts remain to be validated.

title: A Cerebellar Radiomics Model Based on Automatic Segmentation and SHAP-Interpretable Machine Learning for Parkinson's Disease Discrimination
abstract: Abstract Background Parkinson's disease (PD) is among the most common progressive neurodegenerative disorders, and early and accurate identification is vital for effective subsequent treatment interventions. Recent pathological and neurophysiological research has clearly demonstrated the cerebellum's significant role in PD's pathological progression. This study utilizes automatic segmentation techniques to investigate the potential of radiomics methods, based on cerebellar MRI images, for distinguishing between PD patients and healthy control (HC) individuals. Methods This study retrospectively gathered and analyzed 3DT1WI images from 377 subjects in the PPMI database. Fastsurfer segmentation was employed to identify four cerebellar regions of interest (ROIs): left and right gray matter, and left and right white matter. From each ROI, 833 radiomic features were independently extracted. Subjects were randomly assigned to training and testing sets in a 7:3 ratio. Following preprocessing and feature selection, various machine learning algorithms were used for modeling and evaluation, with the best-performing model selected for SHAP visualization. Results Nine radiomic features were ultimately chosen for modeling. The best model, developed using the logistic regression (LR) algorithm, achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.774 in the training set and 0.714 in the testing set. SHAP visualization indicated that the feature 47_wavelet_LHH_glcm_Imc2 contributed most significantly to differentiating PD. Conclusion This study, based on 3DT1WI imaging data, extracted radiomic features from the left and right gray and white matter of the cerebellum and successfully constructed a radiomic model to differentiate between PD patients and HC individuals. The model effectively captures the heterogeneous characteristics of cerebellar gray and white matter, highlighting potential pathological changes in PD patients and offering valuable support for PD diagnosis.

title: Clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway, treatment patterns, and survival among women with cytologically diagnosed breast cancer in two national referral hospitals in Niger: A five- year retrospective multicenter cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer is the leading cancer among women worldwide, with disproportionately high mortality in low- and middle-income countries due to delayed diagnosis and limited access to comprehensive care. Contemporary data describing breast cancer management in Niger remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway, treatment patterns, and survival of women with breast cancer managed in the country's two national referral hospitals. Methods We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study including women with breast cancer diagnosed by fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC), with or without subsequent histopathological confirmation, between January 2020 and December 2024 at the National Cancer Control Center (CNLC) of Niamey and the Issaka Gazoby Maternity Hospital(MIG). Duplicate records were identified and merged using the unique national identification number assigned by the National Cancer Control Center, ensuring that each patient was included only once. Demographic, clinicopathological, treatment, and follow-up data were extracted from medical records. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier product-limit method from the date of cytological diagnosis to death or censoring. Patients alive at five years, alive at the last documented contact, or lost to follow-up were censored at their last known date alive. Results A total of 674 women were included. The median age was 45 years (interquartile range: 35–53), and 70.0% presented with AJCC Stage III-IV disease after a median consultation delay of 7 months. Although FNAC established the diagnosis in all patients, only 25.5% underwent histopathological confirmation, and no patients received immunohistochemical characterization. Modified radical mastectomy was the predominant surgical procedure, and chemotherapy was administered to most patients, whereas radiotherapy and endocrine therapy remained available to only about one-third of women. During follow-up, 10.4% died and 28.5% were lost to follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly poorer overall survival among women presenting with advanced-stage disease (log-rank P < 0.001). Conclusions Breast cancer in Niger is characterized by delayed presentation, advanced-stage disease, and major deficiencies in pathological diagnosis despite universal access to cytological confirmation. Limited availability of histopathology, immunohistochemistry, radiotherapy, and long-term follow-up constrain delivery of guideline-concordant care. Strengthening early diagnosis, expanding pathology and molecular diagnostic services, reducing financial barriers, and improving continuity of care should be priorities for breast cancer control in Niger and similar resource-constrained settings.

title: Fragmented ownership and multilevel barriers to breast MRI screening among high-risk women: A qualitative study informing development of clinical decision support
abstract: Abstract Background: Women at high risk for breast cancer include those with pathogenic variants in hereditary breast cancer predisposition genes, high-risk benign breast lesions, or a lifetime risk over 20% based on validated models. Supplemental breast MRI screening improves early detection and reduces interval cancers in high-risk women. Despite recommendations from professional organizations for breast MRI screening among high-risk women, uptake remains low. To better understand breast MRI utilization, we conducted a qualitative study exploring healthcare provider and patient perspectives to inform development of a screening module within our patient-facing web-based decision aid, RealRisks . Methods: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 women at high risk for breast cancer and 17 healthcare providers at an urban academic medical center in New York City. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and coded using Dedoose software. Transcripts were analyzed thematically to identify patterns in clinician communication strategies, MRI screening practices, as well as barriers and facilitators shaping implementation. Results: All enrolled providers were female, including six primary care providers (PCPs), five gynecologists, four breast radiologists, and two cancer genetic counselors. Among enrolled patients, mean age was 51.8 years (SD, 14.8) and 40% were Hispanic, 40% non-Hispanic White, 10% non-Hispanic Black, and 10% other. More than half of providers (59%) had ordered a breast MRI for high-risk patients, and 55% of patients had previously undergone MRI screening. The three themes that emerged included: 1) responsibility in initiating MRI screening was fragmented across specialties; 2) patients and providers encountered barriers at every step of the screening process, including knowledge gaps and uncertainty about insurance coverage; 3) both groups identified a need for clearer, consolidated guidelines and accessible resources to support informed decision-making. Conclusion: Our findings highlight the need to address structural and communication barriers to improve MRI screening uptake among high-risk women and their providers . Integrating electronic medical record (EMR)-based risk assessment and patient educational materials into clinical workflows may support informed, shared decision-making. Future work will involve design and usability testing of the RealRisks screening module, which will be available in English and Spanish and tailored to patients with varying health literacy and educational backgrounds.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted prediction of Xpert-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis using routine clinical and laboratory data in Southern Zambia: a retrospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence has shown promise for tuberculosis screening, particularly through automated chest radiograph interpretation. Its usefulness when applied to routinely collected clinical and laboratory data in district-level African settings is less certain. We assessed whether simple machine-learning models could predict Xpert-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis using routine surveillance data from a clinical laboratory in Southern Zambia. Methods We performed a retrospective pilot prediction study using tuberculosis surveillance records from Namwala District Hospital and referring facilities. Records without a valid GeneXpert result were excluded, and duplicate study numbers were reduced to one diagnostic episode. The outcome was Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected versus not detected by Xpert MTB/RIF. Descriptive comparisons, univariable logistic regression and a parsimonious multivariable model were undertaken. Logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting models using body mass index and specimen type were evaluated with repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (20 repeats). Model performance was described by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision-recall AUC and Brier score. Bootstrap internal validation was used for the final logistic model. Results Of 129 records, 8 lacked a GeneXpert outcome and 3 duplicate records were removed, leaving 118 unique diagnostic episodes. MTB was detected in 17 patients (14.4%, 95% CI 9.2–21.9). Median age was 30 years, 63 (53.4%) participants were male, 42 (35.6%) were HIV positive and 95 (80.5%) were inpatients. Saliva-labelled specimens were positive in 4 of 7 cases (57.1%), compared with 13 of 109 non-saliva specimens (11.9%). Saliva remained associated with MTB detection after adjustment for body mass index (adjusted OR 10.55, 95% CI 2.09–53.37; P = 0.004), although the estimate was imprecise. Cross-validated AUROC was 0.593 for logistic regression, 0.522 for random forest and 0.596 for gradient boosting. The final logistic model had an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.666 and Brier score of 0.121. Conclusions Routine clinical and laboratory variables had limited ability to predict Xpert-confirmed tuberculosis in this small real-world dataset. The association with saliva-labelled specimens is hypothesis-generating and requires verification. The models are not suitable for clinical deployment or exclusion of patients from molecular testing. Larger, prospectively curated, multicentre Zambian datasets are required before artificial intelligence can support tuberculosis diagnostic prioritisation in routine care.

title: Prognostic Value of Baseline High-Resolution CT Imaging Features for Clinical Cure in Pulmonary Disease Caused by the Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare Complex
abstract: Abstract Objective: To investigate the baseline chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) imaging characteristics of patients with pulmonary disease caused by the Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex (MAC-PD) and to evaluate their predictive value for clinical cure. Methods: For this retrospective analysis, we included 158 patients with MAC-PD who received treatment at two institutions—Beijing Chest Hospital (Capital Medical University) and The Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital (University of South China)—over the 5-year period from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025. Baseline HRCT images were collected and evaluated for imaging signs including bronchiectasis, nodules, cavities, tree-in-bud patterns, consolidation, and fibrosis, as well as the extent of pulmonary involvement.All participants were placed on a standardized anti-MAC therapeutic regimen. Treatment response was then used to assign patients to either the cured or non-cured category. Radiologic features were compared across these two outcome groups, and a multivariate logistic model was constructed to evaluate the association between baseline imaging findings and failure to achieve clinical cure. Results: Among the 158 patients, 102 (64.6%) achieved clinical cure, while 56 (35.4%) did not. The most common HRCT findings in MAC-PD were nodules (84.2%), bronchiectasis(79.7%),cavities (55.1%),and tree-in-bud signs (51.3%).Multilobar involvement,defined as involvement of three or more lobes, was observed in 113 patients (71.5%).The HRCT composite score yielded an AUC of 0.845 for predicting treatment failure. On univariate comparison, the non-cured group exhibited significantly higher rates of cavitation (69.6% vs. 44.1%, P=0.002), more extensive nodular involvement (3.3±1.5 vs. 2.2±1.2 lobes), and more extensive bronchiectasis (3.6±1.7 vs. 2.4±1.4 lobes) than did the cured group. Multivariate analysis further identified three baseline imaging features as independent predictors of non-cure: cavitation (OR=4.12, 95% CI: 2.01–8.45), nodular disease involving ≥3 lobes (OR=2.61, 95% CI: 1.31–5.20), and bronchiectasis involving ≥3 lobes (OR=2.35, 95% CI: 1.14–4.85). Conclusions: MAC-PD is characterized on HRCT predominantly by nodules, bronchiectasis, cavities, and tree-in-bud signs, frequently presenting as a triad of nodules, cavities, and bronchiectasis. Baseline cavitation and extensive disease involvement were identified as independent risk factors for reduced clinical cure rates. The quantitative HRCT scoring approach yielded robust prognostic performance in this MAC-PD cohort, with an AUC of 0.845 supporting its utility as a reliable predictor of treatment response.

title: Acute shoulder gouty arthritis complicated by partial rotator cuff tear misdiagnosed as calcific tendinitis: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Acute shoulder gout concurrent with rotator cuff injury is extremely rare in clinical practice. This disease presents non-specific clinical manifestations and conventional imaging features, resulting in a high misdiagnosis rate. Relevant clinical studies remain limited. We report a typical case herein, summarize the core causes of misdiagnosis, and refine standardized diagnostic and therapeutic principles, aiming to provide evidence-based references for precise clinical diagnosis and management of similar conditions. Case presentation A 52-year-old male patient presented with abrupt severe right shoulder pain lasting 2 days. He had a long-standing history of gout involving the first metatarsophalangeal and knee joints with poorly controlled serum uric acid. Laboratory tests revealed significantly elevated serum uric acid and systemic inflammatory markers. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) initially indicated calcific tendinitis, and symptoms failed to resolve after routine conservative treatment. Arthroscopic exploration revealed extensive chalky white monosodium urate (MSU) crystal deposition on the acromial and tendinous surfaces, combined with a partial supraspinatus tendon tear. Intraoperative synovectomy, thorough crystal debridement, and rotator cuff repair were performed. Postoperative histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of shoulder gouty arthritis. Standard long-term urate-lowering therapy was administered postoperatively, achieving significant pain relief. At the 3-month follow-up, serum uric acid was stably controlled, and full shoulder function was recovered. Conclusion Acute shoulder gout combined with rotator cuff tear is a rare clinical entity that is frequently misdiagnosed as calcific tendinitis. High clinical suspicion for shoulder gout should be maintained in patients with hyperuricemia or a gout history presenting with acute severe shoulder pain. Arthroscopic debridement combined with rotator cuff repair, followed by standardized long-term urate-lowering therapy and adjuvant traditional Chinese medicine intervention, can substantially improve long-term clinical outcomes.

title: CT and Ultrasound Diagnosis of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm with Chronic Torsion: A Case Report with Systematic Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN) is an uncommon appendiceal tumor whose chronic torsion has not been well characterized on imaging. A 48-year-old woman with an incidentally detected right lower quadrant mass underwent serial CT and ultrasound examinations over 3.5 years. Baseline imaging in 2022 showed a thin-walled tubular cystic structure with an early whirl sign at the appendiceal base. By 2024, the wall had thickened with faint calcification while the whirl sign persisted. In 2026, the patient presented with acute right lower quadrant pain; CT demonstrated nodular wall calcification and periappendiceal fat stranding that obscured the whirl sign, while ultrasound revealed a snowstorm echotexture without detectable mural flow. Emergency laparoscopy confirmed 720-degree clockwise torsion with mid-to-distal necrosis. Pathology confirmed LAMN confined to the mucosa and muscularis propria with negative margins. This case illustrates that progressive wall thickening and calcification on serial CT, combined with ultrasound, can identify chronic torsion even when classic signs are masked by superimposed inflammation.

Emergency laparoscopy confirmed 720-degree clockwise torsion with mid-to-distal necrosis. Pathology confirmed LAMN confined to the mucosa and muscularis propria with negative margins. This case illustrates that progressive wall thickening and calcification on serial CT, combined with ultrasound, can identify chronic torsion even when classic signs are masked by superimposed inflammation.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Digital Periapical Radiography and Cone- Beam Computed Tomography for Assessment of Intrabony Periodontal Defects
abstract: Abstract Background Assessment of intrabony periodontal defects is at the heart of diagnosis, prognosis and treatment planning. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) allows three-dimensional visualization; however, digital intraoral periapical radiography (IOPA) is still the most common modality used in clinical practice because it is generally more accessible, less expensive and associated with lower radiation. While CBCT provides a better three-dimensional characterization, previous papers have reported a similar linear measurement accuracy for these imaging modalities. Objectives To compare the accuracy and agreement of digital intraoral periapical radiography (IOPAR) with cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) in the linear and angular measurement of intrabony periodontal defects. Methods This is a comparative cross-sectional study that was performed on 36 patients with intrabony periodontal defects. Standardised digital IOPA and CBCT images for defect height, depth, width and angle measurements were taken. Agreement between modalities was assessed using paired t-tests, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results No statistically significant differences existed between IOPA and CBCT for any parameter (p > 0.05). There were no clinically meaningful mean differences for height (− 0.10 mm), depth (− 0.18 mm), width (0.02 mm) and angle (− 0.50°). The ICC values were good to excellent, ranging from 0.87 to 0.93. Bland–Altman analysis indicated acceptable levels of bias (most observations within the 95% limits of agreement). Conclusions The linear and angular measurements of intrabony periodontal defects obtained using digital intraoral periapical radiography were comparable to those obtained using CBCT. CBCT remains superior for three-dimensional assessment of complex defect morphology and should be used selectively when additional anatomical information is likely to influence treatment planning. These findings support digital intraoral periapical radiography as an accessible, cost-effective, and lower-radiation modality for routine periodontal assessment.
